matchmaking_overlay.instrumentation_detail: OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION|PROCESS_VM_READ) + VirtualQueryEx + ReadProcessMemory, only when the operator presses ENTER in the capture window. One press now takes two read-only captures: the decrypted PE sections, and a walk of the whole address space - every committed readable region, not only the sections. No debugger, no injection, no thread suspension, nothing written into the game and nothing loaded into it. If the operator never presses ENTER, nothing touches fifa15.exe at all.
matchmaking_overlay.instrumentation_why: Denuvo decrypts .xtext lazily, page by page, only as code executes. The 2026-08-15 dumps are decrypted for their first third and sit at entropy 8.00 past 50% because those paths had never run, and their .rdata came out empty. The lobby code is only readable while the lobby is actually stuck, which is a moment only the operator can identify. The section dumps were repeated on 2026-08-18 and contained zero readable program strings both times; the address-space walk then found them in a section the dumper never requested, .reloc a, which is plaintext on disk as well as in memory. The strings therefore never needed a live capture; .xtext, the code, still does, because it is encrypted on disk and decrypts lazily as paths execute.

matchmaking_overlay.lead12_basis: A bandwidth reply is NOT a verbatim echo, which is what v10 assumed. Across all ten captured request/reply pairs retail rewrites two fields: index at bytes 12-16 is the request index PLUS ONE big-endian, and count at bytes 16-20 is the same value rewritten little-endian. The tenth probe is therefore answered with index 10 equal to the count, and that equality is how the client learns the phase finished. We echoed the index unchanged so it never exceeded 9.
